title: Exploring Reduced Precision for Deep Learning Activation Functions
problem: Ultra-low precision formats (FP4, FP3, FP2) remain largely unexplored for activation functions in neural networks, despite success in tensor operations. Understanding the viability of reduced-precision activations is critical for energy efficiency and memory optimization.
motivation: Modern hardware supports FP16/FP8, but activation functions—critical for model convergence—are typically computed in higher precision, wasting memory bandwidth and energy. Ultra-low precision activations could unlock significant hardware efficiency gains.
method: Develop PyTorch framework to emulate and train models with activation functions computed in FP8, FP6, FP4, FP3, and FP2. Conduct comprehensive experiments across multiple models and datasets to assess accuracy degradation at each precision level.
key_novelty: Systematic evaluation of ultra-low precision (FP2-FP4) activation functions across diverse model architectures; identification of FP4 as practical lower bound and precision-dependent behavior of piecewise-linear vs. smooth activations.
contributions: PyTorch framework for reduced-precision activation function emulation during training
Comprehensive evaluation across FP8, FP6, FP4, FP3, FP2 precision levels
Finding that piecewise-linear activations (ReLU variants) maintain 40-83% accuracy at FP2
Identification of FP4 as practical lower bound for most activation functions
limitations: Evaluation scope limited to specific activation function types; inference performance not addressed; hardware-specific quantization considerations not explored.
